question.text: A Category III AIF proposes to issue units with a 'priority distribution model' where Class A investors receive higher share of profits ahead of Class B, effectively at the cost of Class B. Per the recent SEBI circular referenced in the chapter, the Investment Manager:

answer.text: Can proceed freely since unit-class differentiation is at the Manager's discretion
Cannot adopt such a priority-distribution model in Cat III AIFs (effectively barred under the SEBI circular)
Must only notify SEBI before issuance
Can proceed if at least 51% of Class A investors approve

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 14.12 closing note, 'as per recent SEBI Circular, no Category III AIF can adopt such a priority distribution model, in which one class of investors are getting a higher share of profits at the cost of another class of investors.' The bar applies to Cat III; broader SEBI guidance in 2022-23 also restricted this for Cat I/II. The Trap: Option A ignores the SEBI bar. Option C and D under-state the SEBI position. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B highlights this from a distribution-marketing angle. XIX-C tests the manager's duty to NOT design such structures in the PPM in the first place. Manager's Pro-Tip: Review legacy PPMs for any language even resembling priority-waterfall across investor classes. Grandfathering for pre-circular structures is limited — legal review with the AIF's lawyer at each annual PPM-refresh cycle is the safe playbook.
